summary: Answer: probably yes, deep inside. Scientists think extreme pressure turns carbon into diamonds that sink. Uranus ~2.4 light-hours away, tipped ~98 degrees; Neptune ~4 light-hours, winds ~2,000 km/h. Only Voyager 2 ever visited. Next stop: beyond Neptune, a possible ninth planet.

scenes.narration: Scientists think it rains diamonds out here.
The answer: probably yes, deep inside Uranus and Neptune.
Crushing pressure squeezes carbon into diamonds, which sink like hailstones.
Uranus is about two and a half light-hours from us at its closest.
It's tipped on its side, spinning at ninety-eight degrees.
So its poles get forty-two years of sunlight, then forty-two years of darkness.
Neptune sits about four light-hours away, in the cold and dark.
Its winds hit about two thousand kilometers per hour. The fastest in the solar system.
Only one spacecraft ever visited, Voyager Two, in nineteen eighty-six and eighty-nine.
It flew past both planets in a few hours, then kept going.
Beyond Neptune, odd orbits hint that something huge might be hiding.
Next stop, the outer dark. Is a ninth planet hiding there? Yes or no?
